anchors.paper_title: Working memory processes and intrinsic motivation: An EEG study
anchors.reason: Same authors (Zhozhikashvili, Protopova, Shkurenko, Arsalidou, Zakharov) and Sternberg task EEG study with varying difficulty; the study paper reports this dataset's data (N=48).

metadata.methods_description: Participants performed a Sternberg task during EEG recording. Each trial had a 500-1000 ms fixation cross, then 1500 ms encoding, 2000 ms retention, and 1500 ms retrieval (probe letter). Participants answered yes or no with arrow keys. There were 200 trials in total, 40 per set size, in random block order with equal numbers of positive and negative probes. Stimuli were presented with Psychopy2. Triggers mark only stimulus onset, so retention and retrieval onsets must be computed from the trial design (1500 ms and 3500 ms after the trigger).

citation_details.title: Dynamic calibration of self-efficacy to cognitive load: the longitudinal mediation effect of state anxiety
citation_details.author: Xiaolong Li, Mu Xia
citation_details.abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous research has shown that higher self-efficacy predicts lower cognitive load. Nevertheless, there is limited research exploring the dynamic calibration phenomenon of cognitive resources by self-efficacy during task execution through experimental methods. METHODS: This study elucidates the relationships and longitudinal mediating effects among self-efficacy, state anxiety, and cognitive load through two studies that employed convenience sampling. Study 1, which aims to provide a comprehensive theoretical understanding of the research question, is an interview study that examines the prevalence of fluctuations in self-efficacy among 22 university students through an in-depth interview. On the other hand, study 2 reveals further causal relationships through experimental methods. citation_details.title: Factors influencing self-regulated learning ability among Medical undergraduates in China: a cross-sectional study
citation_details.author: Jinmeng Huang, Chunxia Huang, Jian Qin, Kaiyong Huang
citation_details.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-regulated learning (SRL) is the core purpose of lifelong learning and the precondition for medical staff to continuously adapt to and excel in their current and future positions. Good SRL abilities positively impact the academic performance and clinical skills of medical students. Despite its importance, the factors influencing SRL among medical students in China remain under-explored. This study investigates these factors among Chinese medical undergraduates. METHODS: This cross-sectional survey was conducted among a convenience sample of undergraduate students at all four medical universities in Guangxi, using a questionnaire developed and tailored by Zude Zhu. Responses from 2,179 Chinese medical undergraduate students were included in the analyses. citation_details.abstract: Purpose Driven by global sustainable development goals, this study addresses a gap in understanding the core motivation of Executive social responsibility (ESR) for enterprise Green innovation (GI), which has been overlooked in prior institutional and resource-based view studies. In addition, the present research explores the insufficiently investigated interaction between ESR and external stakeholders' pressure. Design/methodology/approach Based on Upper Echelons Theory and Stakeholder Theory, this study empirically examines the proposed mechanism using survey data collected from 283 manufacturing enterprises. citation_details.title: A Psychophysiological Investigation of Boredom Profiles Differing in Meaning, Stimulation and Subsequent Activity Choices
citation_details.author: Konrad Rudnicki, Koen Rummens, Heidi Vandebosch, Jolien De Schepper, Karolien Poels
citation_details.abstract: This study investigated the psychophysiological markers of distinct boredom profiles, defined along the meaning and stimulation dimensions of the Meaning and Attention Components (MAC) model. Psychophysiological markers were also assessed during regulatory activity choices following boredom to investigate their actual regulatory potential. The study ( N = 60, M age = 21.4, SD = 3.38, male = 35%) employed a mixed-factorial design, with meaning as a between-subjects factor and stimulation level as a within-subjects factor in a boring task. Electrodermal activity (EDA), as well as alpha and theta EEG frequencies, were recorded both during the task and during the subsequent activity choices (i.e., switching or adapting the boring task). citation_details.title: What masking geometry works best for EEG foundation models?
citation_details.author: Pierre Guetschel, Bruno Aristimunha, Yassine El Ouahidi, Arnaud Delorme A, Thomas Moreau, Michael Tangermann
citation_details.abstract: EEG foundation models hold promise for scalable brain-signal decoding across clinical and cognitive neuroscience applications, yet their pre-training pipelines remain poorly understood. Among design choices, the masking strategy is particularly critical: it determines what the network must predict and from which context. Yet it has never been ablated in isolation, as each new model bundles a new masking strategy with a new backbone and objective. In this paper, we formalize the design choices for spatio-temporal masking strategies and train various models with a single pipeline under varying masking configurations across two SSL frameworks (MAE and JEPA). We then systematically evaluate the resulting 58 pre-trained models on the 12 datasets of OpenEEGBench under a linear probe. Both frameworks agree on an optimal masking configuration and on shared failure modes. Outside these, performance is robust: 11 MAE and 9 JEPA configurations are statistically indistinguishable from the best. We further identify a novel JEPA-specific failure mode, tagged bias-inflation collapse, invisible to standard detectors. With a well-chosen mask, our pipeline reaches REVE-level downstream performance at a fraction of REVE's pre-training compute.

citation_details.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
citation_details.author: Ryota Kanai C
citation_details.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.
